templates.name: Meeting notes
templates.prompt:
Write meeting notes.
- In overview, give the purpose and outcome in 3–6 sentences.
- "Agenda" section (bullets): one line per topic discussed.
- "Decisions" section (bullets): only what was agreed or settled. Leave out anything discussed but not decided.
- "To-dos" section (checklist): only concrete actions someone agreed to take. Fill owner and due only when they were said.
- Skip any section with nothing to put in it.

templates.name: Brief
templates.description: A 3–5 sentence overview and the key points
templates.prompt:
Write a short summary that reads fast.
- In overview, cover everything in 3–5 sentences.
- Make a single "Key points" section (bullets): 3–7 items, one sentence each, most important first.
- Leave out details and small talk.

templates.name: To-dos
templates.description: Everything to do, with owners and due dates
templates.prompt:
Focus on what needs to happen next.
- In overview, say in one or two sentences what the conversation was about.
- "To-dos" section (checklist): every concrete action someone agreed to take, written as "do something". Fill owner and due only when they were said.
- "To check" section (bullets): only if something is still undecided or needs looking into.
- If there are no to-dos, leave sections empty and say so in overview.

templates.name: Lecture notes
templates.description: Concepts, definitions, examples and questions, ready to study
templates.prompt:
Turn the lecture or seminar into study notes.
- In overview, give the topic and key message in 2–4 sentences.
- "Key concepts" section (bullets): new concepts and terms as "term: definition".
- "Examples" section (bullets): examples and cases used in the explanation.
- "Q&A" section (bullets): questions and answers as "Q. … → A. …".
- "Further reading" section (bullets): references mentioned or things to study next.
- Skip any section with nothing to put in it.

templates.name: Interview
templates.description: Answers by question and memorable quotes
templates.prompt:
Organize the interview by question.
- In overview, say who it was with, what it was about, and the biggest finding in 2–4 sentences.
- One section (bullets) per question asked: the heading is the question, the items are the points of the answer.
- Finally, a "Quotes" section (bullets): memorable things the other person said, quoted briefly without changing the meaning.
- If clear follow-ups came up, add a "Follow-ups" section (checklist).

templates.name: Ideas
templates.description: Pros, cons and next steps for each idea
templates.prompt:
Organize the brainstorm.
- In overview, give the topic and the most promising direction in 2–4 sentences.
- One section (bullets) per idea: the heading is the idea's name, and items start with "What:", "Pros:", or "Concerns:". Skip what nobody said.
- Finally, a "Next steps" section (checklist): only things the group decided to try. Fill owner and due only when they were said.
